By this common award, both the claim petitions, based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) and arising out of same accident, filed under section 166/140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, would be decided.
2. Important facts of the case are as under.

Shweta Jain died and her husband Neeraj Jain suffered injury on account of a motor vehicular accident, took place on 01/05/2021, at around 10.10 p.m, at Near Shakarpur Bus Stop, Opposite Heera Sweets.

In connection with this accident, an FIR No.
159/21, u/S 279/337/304A IPC, was also registered at PS Shakarpur on the complaint of injured Neeraj Jain.

As per the FIR, at the aforesaid time, the petitioner alongwith his wife was going to Shani Dev temple on a scooty bearing No. DL13SA4808 and when they reached at Shakarpur bus stop opposite Heera Sweets, R1 came there driving the offending truck bearing No. HR69B9350 in a very rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty of the petitioner.

Due to the impact, both petitioners and his wife fell down on road and wife of the petitioner came MACP No.351/2021,

3. At the time of filing of DAR, all the respondents marked appearance.
R3 filed written statement but despite last opportunity granted to R1 and R2 to file written statement, no reply was filed by them.

R3 has stated that offending vehicle was insured with R3 in the name of R2 and further that there appear to be false implication of the alleged offending vehicle, whereas negligence was on the part of the driver of the victim vehicle i.e. petitioner.
Petitioner had not provided any DL to IO and this shows he did not have a valid driving licence.
Petitioner has alleged that offending truck hit scooty from behind whereas other witnesses have stated, it hit the scooty from side.
The victim vehicle was in offroad condition as per mechanical inspection report, contrary to the stand taken by the petitioner regarding he having driven the scooty after the accident.
The offending vehicle was being MACP No.351/2021, Neeraj Jain & Anr. v. Tehseen & Ors.

8. Issue wise findings in both of the cases are as hereunder: MACP No. 351/21 & 352/21 ISSUE No.1 :
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
10. The involvement of aforesaid truck in the accident is not in dispute.
Admittedly, the FIR was registered without MACP No.351/2021, Neeraj Jain & Anr. v. Tehseen & Ors.

Petitioner is an eye witness, who has clearly deposed regarding the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
He was not subjected to crossexamination by any of the respondents.
No reply to the claim petitions was filed by respondent no. 1 and 2 in any of the claim petitions.
Chargesheet was filed against R1 after investigation in the connected criminal case.
Ld. Counsel for R3 argued that the eye witness was himself negligent as he craned his neck to look on the back side.
However, this argument does not hold any water.
PW1 has clearly testified that he had slightly turned his neck on hearing loud noise of the truck coming from back side.
Hence, at best, his act can be seen as a precautionary measure to remain on guard and save himself in the nick of time, which unfortunately petitioner Neeraj Jain could not manage.

It is the duty of driver of a vehicle to maintain safe distance from the vehicles moving ahead of it and in this case, truck driver was driving at a fast speed and then hit on the victim's scooty while driving so.
11.

On considering the aforesaid testimony of sole eye witness, the police investigation report and the supporting material on record, it is found that the manner of accident and involvement of offending vehicle are duly proved.

sentences.text: The offending vehicle and victim vehicle were seized on the very next day of accident.
In response to the notice U/s 133 MV Act, R2 had stated to the IO that on 01/05/2021, his driver Tehseen/R1 was driving the said vehicle.
R1 has not disputed this fact and no reply was filed by R1.
The MLC of deceased Shweta Jain reflect that she was declared brought dead and alleged history of road traffic accident was reported to the doctor by her husband/petitioner Neeraj.

Further, the postmortem report of deceased Shweta Jain, filed along with the DAR reflects that she died because of "haemorrage and shock consequent to antemortem injuries and all injuries are fresh in duration prior to death and caused by blunt force sarface impact".
The mechanical inspection report of the victim scooty shows accidental impact and several fresh damages were noted.
The mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle also bore signs of accidental impact and several fresh damages on front body of the truck were found.
These corroborate the version of PW1.
Further, MLC of petitioner Neeraj Jain prepared at Lok Nayak Hospital shows that he had suffered grievous injuries in the road accident.

13. In view of this Court, aforesaid material is found sufficient to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1 MACP No.351/2021, Neeraj Jain & Anr. v. Tehseen & Ors. MACP No.352/2021, Neeraj Jain v. Tehseen &
Ors.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
10. The involvement of aforesaid truck in the accident is not in dispute.
